recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Introduce a 2 and use the product formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. Multiplying and dividing by 2 lets 2 cosA cosB = cos(A+B) + cos(A−B) be applied, turning a product into a sum.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply and divide by 2 so that 2cosA cosB = cos(A+B) + cos(A−B) can turn the product into a sum.

recall.must_convey: That a 2 is introduced so 2cosA cosB = cos(A+B) + cos(A−B) applies, giving (1/2)[cos60° + cos36°].
accept: multiply and divide by two then use two cos A cos B equals cos of the sum plus cos of the difference
introduce a two so the product formula applies, giving cos sixty plus cos thirty six
turn the product into a sum of cosines
two techi product formula vaadali, cos sixty plus cos thirty six vasthundi
convert the product to a sum

steps.why: The formula needs a 2 in front, and there is none — so one is manufactured and paid for with the 1/2 outside.
common_mistakes: Applying the formula without the 2 and being out by a factor.

steps.label: Substitute the exact values
steps.margin_note: Second mark. cos60° = 1/2 and cos36° = (√5+1)/4 — the second is a standard result and is quoted, not derived.
steps.memory_tip: cos60° = 1/2 and cos36° = (√5 + 1)/4 — the second is standard and is quoted.

recall.must_convey: That cos60° = 1/2 and cos36° = (√5+1)/4 are substituted, giving (3+√5)/8.
accept: cos sixty is a half and cos thirty six is root five plus one over four giving three plus root five over eight
substitute the exact values and simplify
the answer is three plus root five over eight
cos thirty six ante root five plus one by four, answer three plus root five by eight
combine the fractions to get three plus root five over eight

steps.why: cos36° is one of the pentagon values, like sin18° and sin54°. They are quoted results in this course, not things to derive under exam pressure.
common_mistakes: Adding the fractions without a common denominator.

insider_note: Multiply and divide by 2 to use 2cosA cosB = cos(A+B) + cos(A−B). cos36° = (√5 + 1)/4 has to be quoted — it is not one of the standard-triangle values.
